items.detail: **Wednesday's flash PMIs** are the week's main US data point, the first read on activity since the Fed's hike, with no CPI or jobs report due.
items.why: Strong readings would back the dot plot's case for more hikes and keep yields above 5%.

items.detail: **Trump hosts Xi at the White House Thursday**, with the tariff truce, rare earths and AI export access all on the table.
items.why: A truce extension would relieve chipmakers and the AI names carrying the Nasdaq; a breakdown hits them hardest.

items.detail: **Treasury sells 2-, 5- and 7-year notes Tuesday through Thursday**, with the 10-year yield entering the week just above **5%**.
items.why: After last week's near-failed 20-year sale, weak demand would push yields higher and pressure the Dow again.

items.detail: **Banxico decides Thursday** and Brazil's mid-month inflation lands Friday at a consensus **4.5%**, with the dollar index entering above 100.
items.why: A dollar above 100 keeps emerging market currencies and foreign inflows under pressure whatever local central banks do.

items.detail: **The NSE lists on the BSE Thursday** after its ₹22,562 crore share sale, with the Nifty entering at **23,346** and support at 23,000.
items.why: A strong debut would lift sentiment after six losing weeks; a weak one tests the 23,000 floor.

items.detail: The **Russell 2000** enters the week the weakest major US index, and **Wednesday's PMIs** decide whether rate-sensitive small caps keep lagging.
items.why: Bank of America reckons each 25bp hike cuts about 2% from Russell 2000 earnings.

items.detail: **Bitcoin** enters near **$81,000** after ETFs took in $433 million on Friday, facing resistance it has failed at twice this month.
items.why: Clearing $83,000 needs the inflows to continue; Wednesday's PMIs are the main thing that could stop them.

items.detail: **Ether** starts near **$2,603** with its US ETFs still losing money, leaving it reliant on Wednesday's PMIs rather than fund demand.
items.why: Last week's bounce came from short covering, so softer data is now the only obvious buyer.

items.detail: **Monday is the deadline for Solana stakers to move off validators that have not upgraded**, ahead of the Alpenglow activation on September 28.
items.why: SOL enters near $106, and a messy validator migration would undercut the speed story driving it.

items.detail: **Spot gold** enters near **$4,380** after snapping a three-week losing run, with **Wednesday's flash PMIs** the only scheduled test of the inflation story.
items.why: No inflation print is due, so strong PMIs would lift real yields and the dollar against gold.

crossCuttingTheme: Thursday's Trump-Xi summit and Wednesday's flash PMIs bracket the week: the summit decides whether the tariff truce holds, while the PMIs tell markets whether 5% yields and a dollar above 100 have further to run.
